title: Constructible pro-étale sheaves are classical
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a discrete Noetherian ring, $X$ a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme, and $F$ a $\Lambda_X$-module sheaf on $X_{\Proet}$ for which
there is a partition $X=Z_1\sqcup\dots\sqcup Z_n$ into constructible locally
closed subsets such that each restriction $F|_{Z_k}$ to $(Z_k)_{\Proet}$ (reduced
structure) is locally constant of finite type. Then $F$ is classical. The same
holds if such a partition exists only locally on $X$.

proof.text: First establish the one-stratum case, on any scheme. By [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation], each finite constant model of a locally constant finite-type $\Lambda$-module sheaf is finitely presented. Apply [det-pe-finite-local-systems-type] to decompose the scheme into open and closed subschemes $X_M$ on each of which the sheaf is pro-étale locally isomorphic to one fixed $\underline M$, with $M$ finitely presented. It suffices to prove classicality on each $X_M$, by [det-pe-constructible-comparison-local].

source.place: Tag 099Y, lemma-compare-locally-constant, first paragraph of proof; finite-presentation reduction in the paragraph preceding that lemma

proof.text: Work on one $X_M$ and write $E=F|_{X_M}$. The sheaf $T=\mathcal Isom_{\Lambda}(\underline M,E)$ has sections on a pro-étale cover. It is a sheaf: compatible local isomorphisms and their inverses glue sectionwise, with the linearity and inverse identities checked after restriction, by the sheaf equalizer condition in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and the module structures of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The group $H=\mathcal Aut_{\Lambda}(\underline M)$ acts by $h\cdot\varphi=\varphi\circ h^{-1}$; if $\varphi,\psi$ are two sections of $T$, the unique element taking $\varphi$ to $\psi$ is $h=\psi^{-1}\varphi$. Thus $T$ is an $H$-torsor. By clause (3) of [det-pe-finite-local-systems-hom], $H=\nu_{X_M}^*\operatorname{Aut}_{\Lambda}(M)_{X_M,\Et}$. Apply [det-pe-torsor-comparison-glue]: there is an étale covering $\{V_a\to X_M\}$ on which $T$ has sections, hence there are module isomorphisms $e_a:\underline M|_{V_a}\xrightarrow{\sim}E|_{V_a}$.

Here are the descent details in the last sentence of that argument. On $V_a\times_{X_M}V_b$ the transition $e_b^{-1}e_a$ is an isomorphism between pullbacks of the constant étale module sheaf $M$. By [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], comparison inverse image commutes with these scheme pullbacks. Its full faithfulness on module sheaves, [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules], therefore gives a unique étale transition map; its inverse descends too, and faithfulness gives the cocycle identity from $(e_c^{-1}e_b)(e_b^{-1}e_a)=e_c^{-1}e_a$. Identify the étale slice sites with the small sites of the $V_a$ and their intersections using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open]; the equivalence acts on the module operations sectionwise. On pro-étale slices use [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], and use [lem-weil-pbc-site-constant-restriction] on both sites to identify the restrictions of the constant models on every overlap. The covering and all its overlap objects form sets in the site universe. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-gluing] to obtain an étale module sheaf $E_0$ with those constant local models. The local isomorphisms $\nu^*E_0|_{V_a}\cong E|_{V_a}$ agree on overlaps; their maps and inverse maps glue by the sheaf equalizer condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], giving $\nu^*E_0\cong E$. Thus $E$ is classical by [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. Together with step 1 this proves the one-stratum case on every scheme.

source.place: Tag 099Y, lemma-compare-locally-constant, final sentence; explicit gluing of the étale trivializations

proof.text: For a global partition prove the assertion by strong induction on its number $n$ of nonempty strata, simultaneously for all qcqs schemes. If $n=0$, the scheme is empty and its only module sheaf is zero, which is classical by [det-pe-classical-derived-weak-serre]. For $n>0$ and $x\in Z_k$, apply [lem-sf-constructible-partition-local-closed-stratum] to obtain an affine open $W\ni x$ with $Z=Z_k\cap W$ closed and constructible in $W$ and $U=W\setminus Z$ quasi-compact. Put on $Z$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], with inclusions $i:Z\hookrightarrow W$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow W$. This includes $n=1$: the hypothesis then concerns $F|_{X_{\mathrm{red}}}$, so one must not identify that sheaf with $F$ on a nonreduced scheme. The same open–closed argument below handles this case with $U=\varnothing$. The affine $W$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. To check that $U$ is quasi-separated, let $A,B\subseteq U$ be quasi-compact opens. Since $U$ is quasi-compact, their images are quasi-compact opens of the affine scheme $W$, so $A\cap B$ is quasi-compact by the quasi-compact-intersection characterization in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The same argument, with an affine open $A\subseteq W$, shows that $U\cap A$ is quasi-compact; hence the open immersion $j$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible, induction and shrinking about x

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with coefficient ring sheaf $\Lambda_W$ and with $E=F|_W$. This theorem permits an arbitrary sheaf of commutative rings and requires only that the complementary open immersion be quasi-compact, which step 4 proves. Its exact sequence is
$$0\longrightarrow j_!j^*E\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow i_*i^*E\longrightarrow0.$$
The coefficient rings on $U$ and $Z$ are the inverse images of $\Lambda_W$. On the étale sites, [lem-weil-pbc-constant-ring-inverse-image-comparison] gives the corresponding constant-ring isomorphisms for both $j$ and $i$; [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] transports these isomorphisms to the pro-étale pullbacks, using the identification of the pro-étale constant ring with $\nu^*$ of the étale constant ring in [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. The comparison is by ring maps and therefore preserves multiplication and unit. Thus the exact sequence is over precisely the restricted coefficient rings in the statement.

source.place: Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible, short exact sequence; Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open

proof.text: The sets $Z_m\cap U$ for $m\ne k$, after omitting empty ones, partition $U$ into at most $n-1$ constructible locally closed strata. Their constructibility follows from [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-open-restriction]; locally closedness is preserved by taking an open intersection. Each restriction of $F$ is still locally constant with finite models: pull the trivializing cover back to this open subset, retaining the same constant modules, as in [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. Thus the induction hypothesis on the qcqs scheme $U$ gives classicality of $j^*E$. By [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] choose an étale module sheaf $G$ on $U$ and $j^*E\cong\nu_U^*G$.

source.place: Tag 09AK, lemma-compare-constructible, induction for the open part

proof.text:
For this general discrete ring, the extension-by-zero comparison follows directly from adjunction. Restriction to $U$ on the pro-étale site is the slice restriction by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], and its left adjoint $j_!^{\Proet}$ exists for arbitrary coefficient ring sheaves by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. On the étale side use [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. For an étale $V	o U$ and a pro-étale module sheaf $N$ on $W$, the two sheaves $
u_{U,*}j_{\Proet}^*N$ and $j_{\Et}^*
u_{W,*}N$ both evaluate to $N(V	o W)$, with the same maps and scalar actions: this is the direct-image formula of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and the restriction formula of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. The comparison module adjunction is available for every discrete ring by [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. Hence
$$\operatorname{Hom}(
u_W^*j_!^{\Et}G,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G,j_{\Et}^*
u_{W,*}N)=\operatorname{Hom}(G,
u_{U,*}j_{\Proet}^*N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_!^{\Proet}
u_U^*G,N).$$
Uniqueness of left adjoints, [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation], gives $
u_W^*j_!^{\Et}G\cong j_!^{\Proet}
u_U^*G$. Consequently $j_!j^*E$ is classical by [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules].

proof.text: Both ends of the short exact sequence of step 5 are classical by steps 7 and 8. Apply the extension clause of [det-pe-classical-derived-weak-serre] to conclude that $F|_W$ is classical. Such $W$ exist about every $x\in X$ by step 4. Apply [det-pe-constructible-comparison-local] to this open covering to conclude that $F$ is classical. This completes the induction for global finite partitions.

Finally suppose the finite partition is given only locally on $X$. On each open carrying a partition and about each of its points, choose an affine open $V$. Such opens form a basis [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The partition restricts to a finite constructible locally closed partition of $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-open-restriction] and the definition of locally closedness; the local constant models restrict unchanged. The affine $V$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so the global-partition result applies to $F|_V$. These $V$ cover $X$, and [det-pe-constructible-comparison-local] proves the final assertion.
